title: Admin Automation Conductor + Task Templates for Runbook-as-Task
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build an "Automation Conductor" service and a library of idempotent task templates to convert canonical runbooks into executable, auditable tasks. This enables: (1) engineers and support to trigger multi-step admin flows via Slack/CLI/Console, (2) deterministic dry-runs and approvals for high-risk operations, and (3) consistent telemetry and audit trails for post-incident review.

Scope: implement task schema v2 (inputs, validators, compensating actions), a lightweight conductor API that orchestrates k8s jobs and background workers, a templating repo for common admin actions (quota bump, node drain, cache flush, model-rollover), and integrations: Slack command + workflow, PagerDuty runbook links, and GitHub PR gated approvals for destructive tasks.

Acceptance criteria: all items below must be implemented, tested and documented in the internal Runbook-Conductor Confluence page.

Why now: current on-call workflows are ad-hoc; we want reproducible, reviewable, and automated admin operations to reduce MTTR and train junior SREs.

Non-goals: this ticket will not replace full incident automation or advanced playbook synthesis (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Task schema v2 defined and documented (inputs, output schema, error handling, compensation)
Conductor API with POST /tasks, GET /tasks/{id}, and POST /tasks/{id}/approve endpoints implemented
CLI shim (opsctl) and Slack slash command /admin-task that kick off tasks and show progress
3 example task templates committed: node-drain-safe, cache-clear-prefix, model-variant-rollover
Dry-run mode that validates resource-level permissions and performs no destructive changes
Audit trail persisted to internal events-store with trace_id, user, KMS-encrypted params
Integration tests covering happy path, failure + compensation, and retry semantics
Docs: Confluence runbook, Console quicklinks, and a short demo recording in Drive
comments: 2025-11-12 Aisha K: scoped initial MVP. Decided to keep conductor stateless for retries; state persisted in events-store (Postgres).

2025-11-25 Liam C: Prototype CLI that scaffolds task payloads pushed to github.com/redwood-internal/ops-templates (branch feat/conductor-proto). PR: https://github.com/redwood-internal/ops-templates/pull/18
2025-12-08 Eng Sync: trade-off: synchronous vs async approvals. Chose async approvals to allow human review windows; approval flow will be an extra event recorded in the task state.
2026-01-07 QA: added compensation actions requirement after replaying an incident where partial node drains left autoscaler in bad state. Compensation must be idempotent.
2026-01-28 Security review notes: parameters containing customer IDs must be redacted in UI; store originals encrypted with KMS and restrict access via RBAC. Security owner: Sofia Martinez.
2026-02-02 Liam C: integrated Slack prototype into #ops-admin; interactive messages update on task progress. Demo: https://drive.redwood.ai/ops/conductor-demo (internal)
2026-02-10 PM feedback: prefer templates be modular (small composable steps) so Product Support can recompose without engineering changes. Added to scope.
2026-02-12 Aisha K: tagging this ticket for ops-2026.03 release train. Will open follow-up for runbook authoring UI after MVP stabilizes.
notes: Implementation notes: use existing operator-runner infra for k8s job execution to minimize surface area; prefer JSON schema for validators; instrument spans for each template step to correlate with traces in Console. Include a toggle to fallback to manual runbook link for accounts on Dedicated where private tooling is restricted.
